dedupe_keys.name: synxflow gpu flood and landslide simulator

description: SynxFlow simulates flood inundation, landslide runout and debris flow on CUDA-capable graphics processors. The JOSS article describes a Python interface for setup and output analysis, while the own repository documents example hazard simulations. GitHub identifies GPL-3.0 terms, so the code is free. A modeller supplies terrain, forcing and hazard-specific physical parameters; outputs are evolving flow or runout fields. Spatial extent, grid size and simulation period depend on the scenario inputs and hardware. Infrastructure researchers could overlay outputs with roads, buildings or flood defences to assess exposure. That is a downstream use; the software does not provide an authoritative asset inventory. A caveat is that errors in terrain, boundary conditions and material parameters can dominate hazard footprints. GPU availability and memory also limit practical resolution. No directly related catalogue record was confirmed. No example, dataset or installer was downloaded and no simulation was run.
